comments.author: Ebi_Tendon
comments.body:
AI tools right now lack proper testing capabilities. If an AI can’t test its own work, it will only produce incomplete work. That’s different from AI coding, where the AI can validate things with unit tests, integration tests, and E2E tests. But with game engines like Unity, you need much more than that.

For what you’re doing, you need at least a screenshot feature so the AI can verify its own work. But the problem is that current AI systems convert images into text descriptions and then verify the text, because they’re LLMs (Large Language Models). Everything ultimately has to be transformed into text form. That’s one of the current limitations.

I did the screenshot tests, and honestly, they’re still not quite good enough. But for gameplay development, if you can create a playtesting system that lets the AI actually play the game, it works quite well.
